newsitem.title: POLAND: KGHM sale to fund Polish pension rise - minister.
newsitem.headline: KGHM sale to fund Polish pension rise - minister.

text.p: The Polish government will fund part of a more than four percent increase in pensions next year from its partial sale of the KGHM Polska Miedz SA copper combine, Labour Minister Andrzej Baczkowski said on Thursday.

He told parliament the sale would meet costs stemming from a court ruling that the government had to compensate pensioners for a rise they should have received to match pay increases in the last quarter of 1995, PAP news agency reported.
He said the KGHM sell-off was likely to bring between one billion and 1.5 billion zlotys, roughly the amount the Constitutional Tribunal decision would cost the treasury.
Shares in KGHM, one of the world's top copper and silver producers, are expected to hit international and domestic markets at the end of the second quarter of 1997.

The government will initially retain a 51 percent stake in the firm, the value of which is estimated at $2-3 billion, while 34 percent is to be earmarked to the public and 15 percent will go to employees, according to bankers arranging the sale.
In July, the Tribunal ruled that pensions should have been increased in March, as envisaged by the social security law which was effective until the end of 1995.
The law was changed as of January as a prelude to a planned social security reform and the new legislation offered pensioners a 2.5 percent real-term increase this year, payable in September.
But the Tribunal ruled that the rise in pensions and benefits should have been granted in March as it was linked to wage growth in late 1995, when the old law was still effective.
The government has deferred the burden of the extra payment until next year, when it also plans to increase pensions by 1.5 percent -- bringing the total rise to above four percent in real terms.
The court ruling has also been cited by the government as its reason for putting off a personal and corporate income tax cut, promised for next year, until 1998.
Baczkowski said he would present a bill to the government this month on the means of carrying out the Tribunal verdict.
KGHM had a net profit of 481.9 million zlotys last year against 351.1 million in 1994 on sales of 3.72 billion zlotys against 2.69 billion in 1994.
In 1995 it produced 405,739 tonnes of electrolytic copper and 964 tonnes of silver. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
